title: Refactor installer into explicit domains
outOfScope: Provider configuration, secrets, release publication, and adopter project writes are excluded.
Existing installer behavior is preserved; this Work Item does not redesign installation policy.

sources.reason: User-approved WI-12 target domains and compatibility constraints.
Current compatibility CLI and legacy installer implementation.
Existing transaction primitives to preserve and expose through the domain package.

riskAssessment.reason: Moving installer responsibilities can regress compatible command behavior or weaken the read-only plan / approved transaction boundary.

reasons: Installer source and tests change without release publication or provider operations.

executionDecision.reason: The user specified the required domain boundaries and explicitly authorized Contract writes; implementation is repository-local and reversible.

preReviewWarnings: Review compatibility entrypoints and confirm planning remains read-only while transactions require an explicit confirmation.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: scripts/installer exposes named request, inspection, plan, conflict, confirmation, transaction, rollback, ownership, Git-state, evidence, presentation, application, and CLI boundaries.
The compatibility CLI delegates through an application boundary; planning APIs are read-only and transaction execution rejects an unconfirmed plan.
Existing installer CLI command behavior remains covered by focused regression tests.
The installed-lifecycle reference documents the staged compatibility boundary without claiming a provider or release guarantee.
guidelines: New public installer-domain APIs must be documented and tested.
Do not import installer-internal modules from unrelated governance features.
Plans must be read-only and transactions must run only after explicit confirmation.

intent.problem: The legacy installer entrypoint concentrates orchestration, planning, persistence, rollback, and presentation in one module, obscuring which operations are read-only and which may write an adopter repository.
constraints: Do not modify provider configuration or an adopter repository.
Keep plan creation read-only and require explicit confirmation before transaction execution.
Do not rewrite historical Work Item artifacts.
intent.rationale: Explicit installer domains make the trust boundary reviewable without changing the installation policy.

rawUserRequest: Complete WI-12 installer-domain-refactor as part of the user-authorized remediation sequence, preserving installer commands while separating inspection, planning, confirmation, transaction, rollback, ownership, Git facts, evidence, presentation, application, and CLI responsibilities.

declaredIntent.summary: Separate installer responsibilities without weakening command compatibility or the plan/transaction trust boundary.

scenarioCoverage.expected: Inspection and plan creation return data without creating or modifying target files.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run focused installer-domain tests that snapshot the target before and after planning.

scenarioCoverage.expected: An unconfirmed plan is rejected before any transaction callback runs; a confirmed plan may execute only its declared actions.
The compatibility entrypoint delegates through the application boundary and retains existing argument behavior.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run installer entrypoint and installer regression tests.

performanceImpact: The refactor must not add a second installer scan or quality graph; it reuses existing inspection and transaction primitives.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: User explicitly authorized required Contract and governed Work Item writes for this and future Work Items.

rollbackNote: Revert this Work Item diff; the compatibility entrypoint and existing installer policy remain intact.
